item.title: Kyler Murray remained limited in Thursday's practice.
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Carson Wentz is set to start for the Vikings if Murray does not clear the concussion protocol.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was back on the practice field Thursday.

Murray was knocked out of last Sunday's win over the Packers in the first quarter with a concussion and he had made enough progress in his recovery to practice on a limited basis Wednesday. Murray got in another limited session on Thursday and the next update on where he stands in the concussion protocol will come on Friday.

If Murray is not cleared in time to face the Bears, Carson Wentz is in line to start. Wentz was 12-of-19 for 133 yards and three touchdowns after taking over for Murray in Week 1.

Wide receiver Jauan Jennings (personal) and right tackle Brian O'Neill (knee) did not practice. O'Neill was limited on Wednesday while Jennings has not practiced this week.

Linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) was limited for the second straight day and linebacker Blake Cashman (wrist) moved up to full participation.

item.title: Ravens DC Anthony Weaver: Tyler Shough reminds me of "a poor-man's Josh Allen"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Josh Allen's skills were on display in Buffalo's win over the Lions on Thursday night and his performance was the latest reason why any quarterback should be excited about being compared to the Bills star.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen's skills were on display in Buffalo's win over the Lions on Thursday night and his performance was the latest reason why any quarterback should be excited about being compared to the Bills star.

That was where Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver went when he was asked about Saints quarterback Tyler Shough at a Thursday press conference. Weaver said that he believes the "sky's the limit" for the second-year quarterback during an answer that included a comparison to Allen.

"Yes, I like that kid," Weaver said, via a transcript from the team. "We played them towards the latter half of the year when I was in Miami last year, and I was impressed with him then as a rookie. He reminds me a little bit of like a poor-mans Josh Allen. Has all the arm talent in the world [and] can run. I don't think he gets enough credit for how good [of] an athlete he is. So, particularly as you get down to the low red [zone], we are constantly going to be conscious of just his ability to scramble and create those extended plays."

Calling someone a "poor-mans" version of something could be seen as damning with faint praise, but Shough is preparing to make his 11th NFL start so anything that brings Allen to mind is a good sign for where his career can go. A win over the Ravens would be a step toward getting there, but Weaver isn't going to get caught off guard this Sunday.

item.title: Lions score on first drive of second half to close to within 27-17
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Lions aren't dead yet.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions aren't dead yet.

Detroit opened the second half with an 11-play, 74-yard touchdown drive, and now trail the Bills 27-17. The Lions were down 21-0 before Jared Goff hit Jahmyr Gibbs for an 11-yard touchdown. Jake Bates kicked a 31-yard field goal on the last play of the first half, and Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 2-yard touchdown with 9:29 left in the third quarter.

Goff is 18-of-24 for 198 yards and two touchdowns. He has thrown a touchdown in 25 consecutive games.

St. Brown has six catches for 70 yards and a touchdown.

item.title: Dan Campbell: It's a long season, Lions need to get better
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "They got after us, and we didn't play good enough, and we didn't coach good enough. That falls on me," Campbell said.
item.content:encoded:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell saw a lot that his team needs to improve in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Bills.

"We've got a lot of room to grow, and that's encouraging," Campbell said. "We've just got to clean up a lot of things on defense right now, particularly in the back end. . . . It wasn't good enough."

Campbell expressed optimism about the way the Lions can use their extra three days after playing on Thursday night to prepare for Week 3 against the Jets.

"It's early, we're in Week 2, we've got a long season, and the most important thing is that we get better," Campbell said. "We just need to get better than we were today in all three phases. We need to play better against the Jets, and I think we will. We can, and we certainly will."

Campbell credited Bills head coach Joe Brady for having his team ready to play.

"They got after us and we didn't play good enough and we didn't coach good enough. That falls on me," Campbell said. "It certainly needed to be a lot cleaner than that."

item.title: Josh Allen registers 10th game with 2+ rushing, 2+ passing touchdowns
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Steve Young is second on the all-time list, with four.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen is a touchdown machine.

For the 10th time in his career, he has scored two or more rushing touchdowns and two or more passing touchdowns in the same game. His latest score came on the ground from two yards out, extending Buffalo's lead over the Lions to 34-17.

Allen holds the record by a wide margin. In second place on the all-time two-and-two list is Hall of Famer Steve Young. He did it four times.

For the season, Allen has already accounted for nine touchdowns.

Barring a collapse, the Bills will move to 2-0 on the year, with a proper christening of their new stadium.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Josh Allen accounts for five TDs in Bills' 41-31 win over Lions
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bills quarterback threw three touchdowns and ran for two.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen made the first regular-season game in Highmark Stadium memorable for Bills fans.

The quarterback threw three touchdown passes and ran for two in a dominant 41-31 win over the Lions. The Bills improved to 2-0, while the Lions fell to 1-1.

Allen now has four career games with three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns. No other player in NFL history has more than two (Kordell Stewart), according to NFL Researcher.

Allen completed 20 of 31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns. His scoring tosses went for 43 yards to Josh Palmer, 1 yard to Dawson Knox and 16 yards to Dalton Kincaid. Palmer has two catches for 77 yards and two touchdowns this season, having caught the game-winning touchdown in the win over the Texans on Sunday.

Kincaid caught seven passes for a team-leading 95 yards.

The Bills lost wide receiver DJ Moore to a shoulder injury and a stinger in the first half.

Allen also ran for 69 yards and two touchdowns on 14 carries, topped only by James Cook's 21 carries for 135 yards. Cook scored the team's last touchdown on a 1-yard run with 2:50 left to seal it.

The Bills outgained the Lions 446 to 355, were 5-for-5 in the red zone and went 9-of-12 on third down.

Buffalo scored touchdowns on its first four possessions and punted only twice all night.

The Lions, who blew a 21-0 lead to the Saints last week before winning in overtime, fell behind 21-0 and trailed 27-10 at halftime. They twice pulled to within 10 points when the game was still in reach, but Allen and the Bills answered twice.

Detroit's last touchdown, which pulled it to within 10 again, came with 1:42 left as as Amon-Ra St. Brown scored his second touchdown. The Bills, though, recovered the onside kick.

Lions quarterback Jared Goff was 26-of-38 for 327 yards and four touchdowns after a slow start. Goff reached 40,000 yards in his 153rd game, the sixth-fastest for any quarterback.

St. Brown caught nine passes for 142 yards and two touchdowns, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs had 16 carries for 52 yards and caught six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown.

Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, who had two sacks and two forced fumbles in the season-opening win over the Texans on Sunday, had two sacks and a forced fumble against the Lions.

(Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images)

item.title: Josh Allen: Very fortunate to be the QB to open this stadium
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Josh Allen had a lot of big games in the old Highmark Stadium, but it's hard to top the one he came up with for the first game in the new one.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen had a lot of big games in the old Highmark Stadium, but it's hard to top the one he came up with for the first game in the new one.

Allen opened the game with a one-yard touchdown run and then went on to throw three scores while running for another one in a 41-31 win that pushed the Bills to 2-0 on the season. He now has four games with at least three passing touchdowns and two rushing scores in his career and he's the first quarterback with five passing touchdowns and four rushing scores through the first two games of a season.

Those would be special results under any circumstances, but they hit even harder in the first game on a new field. Allen said after the game that being in the spotlight in the new stadium meant something extra to him.

"I think at the national anthem, I caught myself like taking it all in and understanding my job is the coolest thing in the world," Allen said, via the team's website. "It's everything that I've ever wanted to be the quarterback of an NFL franchise. And I'm just very fortunate that I ended up here in Buffalo and got to be the first quarterback to open this stadium. It's a special spot."

No one is calling the new Highmark Stadium "The House that Josh Allen Built" at the moment, but there's little doubt that he'll be the center of attention in every game he plays in the building and they just might come up with a way to name it after him if he can cap off the first season in its history with the first Super Bowl title in franchise history.

item.title: Joe Brady: I wanted to take the ball in that environment and set the tone
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Many teams choose to defer to the second half after winning the coin toss before games, but Bills head coach Joe Brady did not do that on Thursday night.
item.content:encoded:
Many teams choose to defer to the second half after winning the coin toss before games, but Bills head coach Joe Brady did not do that on Thursday night.

Brady elected to take the ball to start the first game at his team's new stadium and that turned out to be a wise move. Running back James Cook ran three times for 23 yards while quarterback Josh Allen completed two passes for 22 yards and ran four times for 40 yards, including a one-yard touchdown to set off a frenzied celebration in the team's new home.

"I've said all along, it was important for us, and I wanted to take the ball in this environment and set the tone," Brady said, via WGR. "I thought we had some good third downs, we finished in the end zone, and that stadium was electric. That was the start that we needed."

Brady was remembering another drive involving third downs because the Bills never faced one on that trip to the end zone, but that's understandable because his team had six touchdown drives over the course of the 41-31 win. All of that success can run together, especially when it plays out to a soundtrack of joyful Bills fans celebrating a memorable night in franchise history.

item.title: Makai Lemon knows he has "lots to improve" after minus-5 yards in his first NFL game
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Eagles rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon had a box score to forget in the first game of his NFL career: Against the Commanders, Lemon caught three passes for minus-5 yards.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon had a box score to forget in the first game of his NFL career: Against the Commanders, Lemon caught three passes for minus-5 yards. Lemon knows he needs to do better.

Lemon caught the first pass thrown to him in the flat for a gain of three yards. The Eagles then twice ran a play when Lemon went in motion and Jalen Hurts threw the ball to him behind the line of scrimmage, and on both he was tackled almost immediately, once for minus-three yards and once for minus-five yards.

“Lots to improve on,” Lemon said, via the Philadelphia Inquirer.

So far, the Eagles don't look like they trust Lemon to get open downfield. In addition to his poor showing in Week 1, in the preseason, Lemon also caught exclusively short passes, finishing with three catches for three yards. Lemon knows he needs to show his team that he can run good downfield routes.

“Route details,” Lemon said. “Just making sure I define my routes and assignments.”

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni defended Lemon and said his game was better than his box score looked.

“There’s a lot of things that Makai did in that game that don’t reflect on the stat sheet,” Sirianni said. “We constantly talk about that: What are you doing to help this team win the game, particularly if you’re a skill guy? That might not be able to be seen from the stat book or to the naked eye. What he’s always done a good job since he’s been here [is] blocking, doing the right things, being in the right spots. Obviously the ones that went to him [on Sunday] didn’t equal out to a big yardage game, right? But he did little things to help us win the football game that sometimes are unseen.”

At some point, though, the Eagles need their first-round receiver to make some plays that do show up on the stat sheet.

item.title: Report: DJ Moore day-to-day with shoulder injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Thursday night was a good night for the Bills on most fronts, but one exception was the shoulder injury that knocked wide receiver DJ Moore out of the game in the second quarter.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday night was a good night for the Bills on most fronts, but one exception was the shoulder injury that knocked wide receiver DJ Moore out of the game in the second quarter.

Moore was ruled out for the rest of the night after halftime and head coach Joe Brady had no update on his condition in his postgame press conference. On Friday morning, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that Moore avoided a major injury and is considered day-to-day moving into Week 3.

The Bills will have extended time before hosting the Chargers on September 27, which should help Moore's chances of making it back into the lineup without missing a game.

Moore did not have a catch before leaving the game, but did run once for one-yard loss. He had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown in Week 1.

item.title: Bo Nix: We're not freaking out about being 0-1
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Broncos opened the regular season with a dud against the Chiefs, but they're not making too much of one result as they prepare for Sunday's home opener against the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos opened the regular season with a dud against the Chiefs, but they're not making too much of one result as they prepare for Sunday's home opener against the Jaguars.

Quarterback Bo Nix threw an interception and lost one of his three fumbles in the 31-10 loss to a divisional rival. He was sacked four times in the game and the Broncos only had 176 total yards of offense, which is the kind of performance that might have some wondering if the offense somehow lost its way on the way into the regular season.

On Thursday, Nix said that's not the case in Denver and that the team still believes they're built the right way for success.

"Overall, we're not going to press the panic button and we're not freaking out," Nix said, via the team's website. "We're not starting from scratch or anything. We feel like we're still in a good spot, we just didn't play great by any means, and we've got to play better."

The Jaguars are coming off a more impressive start, although a home win over the Browns is certainly a different degree of difficulty than a Monday night trip to Arrowhead Stadium. Jacksonville won in Denver last season as well, so the Broncos will have to be much sharper if they're going to avoid a week of listening to stats about how few teams go from 0-2 to making it to the playoffs.

item.title: Jalen Carter to wear a cast on his wrist against the Titans
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter returned to practice on Thursday with a new look.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter returned to practice on Thursday with a new look.

Carter missed Wednesday's practice with a wrist injury and returned to the field wearing a cast on his right wrist. After practice, Carter declined to delve into the details of his injury while telling reporters that he's planning to play against the Titans with the cast on as protection.

“I look fine out there wearing it," Carter said. "Just minor adjustments and I’m still out there practicing and ready to play. . . . I'm still going to have to strike, grab and play the run and pass rush. That's pretty much it. I can't let it affect me."

Carter said he suffered the injury while trying to punch the ball out late in last Sunday's win over the Commanders, but he doesn't plan on letting it interfere too much with the Eagles' bid for a 2-0 start to the season.

item.title: Sean McVay: Myles Garrett is like Wolverine, healing fast, but we won't rush him back
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "I'm reluctant to put a timeline on it. We know that he's going to miss those four weeks at a minimum," McVay said.
item.content:encoded:
Rams coach Sean McVay says defensive end Myles Garrett's knee surgery was successful, but it's too soon to tell when Garrett will be back on the field.

"It went good, he's feeling good, you already see he had crutches yesterday and then he was walking without crutches today. He's like Wolverine, healing fast," McVay said.

That doesn't necessarily mean Garrett will be back on the field on October 18 for the Rams' Week 6 game against the Cardinals, which is the earliest he's eligible to return from injured reserve.

"I'm reluctant to put a timeline on it," McVay said. "We know that he's going to miss those four weeks at a minimum. We're not going to rush him back. We want to make sure he's feeling good, he's able to get on the practice field, do all the things that are necessary for him to perform at a level that he's been accustomed to. I'll keep you guys posted as we have updates, as we go."

Garrett did next to nothing in the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers and can't play for the next four weeks, so the Rams will be about one-third of the way through the season before they get any meaningful contributions for him. That wasn't the plan when they traded for him, but the Rams' top priority is having him ready late in the season and in the playoffs, and McVay sounds confident that will happen.

item.title: Roger Goodell: Europe is the most likely destination for a franchise
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last month, Commissioner Roger Goodell said he has "no doubt" that the NFL will have a team headquartered outside the United States.
item.content:encoded:
Last month, Commissioner Roger Goodell said he has "no doubt" that the NFL will have a team headquartered outside the United States.

Appearing on Prime Video's pregame show before Lions-Bills on Thursday night, Goodell was asked how soon it will happen and where the team would be located.

"You know, that's tough to say," Goodell said. "I think if we continue to grow and continue to get the kind of reaction, I do think a franchise will be international at some point in time. I think Europe is the most likely, for a lot of reasons. One, the length of time we've been playing there. But also the scheduling is going to be a lot easier. Australia might create a few complications for us. But I also believe we could have more than one team. . . . The support is there."

It would make sense to have two teams, especially if the first destination is London, which has two NFL-ready stadiums.

The lingering question is whether current teams would move, or whether the league would expand.

Goodell has in the past hinted at a four-team European division. The best long-term vision could be four teams in Europe and four teams elsewhere (Brazil, Mexico, Australia, and Japan).

Much of that hinges on the return of supersonic flight, a development the NFL is closely monitoring.

Yes, the league has been dangling the carrot of an international team for years. Often, it's about driving interest in the variety-pack of games played in other countries. At this point, it does indeed feel as if it's coming, eventually.

item.title: Emmitt Smith thinks Derrick Henry can break all-time rushing record
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Derrick Henry, at age 32, is playing like he did at age 22.
item.content:encoded:
Derrick Henry, at age 32, is playing like he did at age 22. And he's in position to make a climb up the all-time rushing list.

With 13,163 career yards, could Henry get all the way to the top?

The guy who holds the No. 1 spot — Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith — believes he can.

"Oh yeah, I think it’s possible," Smith said recently, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "Derrick Henry is a bigger back. He takes great care of his body. He's in great shape."

Smith has said he hopes someone breaks the record in his lifetime. He wishes Walter Payton had still been alive when Smith broke the prior record of 16,726 yards.

Currently, Henry trails Smith by 5,193 yards. To get to 18,355, Henry will need to keep rolling for at least four more seasons beyond 2026. That's 84 more games. At an average of 61.8 yards per game, he'll get there.

While Father Time remains undefeated, Henry has been defying it. If he wants to keep going, and if his body holds up, he could get there.

For now, he's only 97 yards behind Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson. With another 403, he'll catch Hall of Famer Jerome Bettis. With 22 more, he'll match Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson. And with 417, he'll tie Hall of Famer Curtis Martin.

In all, Henry is 940 yards away from leapfrogging Dickerson, Bettis, Tomlinson, and Martin. Each of whom are in Canton. Henry will surely get there, too.

Especially if he keeps working his way to the top of the all-time rushing list.

item.title: Sean McVay hopes the Rams never play in Australia again
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: One week ago, the Rams made their debut in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
One week ago, the Rams made their debut in Australia. It didn't go well; the 49ers drubbed the Rams, 27-7.

For that reason, coach Sean McVay hopes the assignment doesn't come their way again.

“It's almost like you try to do the Men in Black thing where you say, ‘Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago,’" McVay told reporters on Thursday. "We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context."

The atmosphere was great. The burden on the teams was not. The strategy of showing up the day before the game ended up being a miscalculation.

Either way, the Rams have 16 games to play. Starting with a visit from the Giants on Monday night.

"Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let's go be about it," McVay said. "Let's go prepare the right way. Let's have great focus and concentration. Let's have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let's go be ready to go against a really damn good football team. What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That's what every week is. We're excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today."

It remains to be seen whether the two long flights with a football game as the Vegemite in the sandwich will affect the Rams in Week 2, or beyond. Either way, an up-and-coming Giants team is coming to town — and thousands of Giants fans in the L.A. area are surely scrambling to buy tickets for the prime-time game at SoFi Stadium.

item.title: Jadarian Price will get more reps moving forward
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In his Week 1 debut, running back Jadarian Price was on the field for only 24 snaps — less than half of the Seahawks' total offensive workload.
item.content:encoded:
In his Week 1 debut, running back Jadarian Price was on the field for only 24 snaps — less than half of the Seahawks' total offensive workload.

That will be changing.

Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury told reporters on Thursday that Price will be getting more playing time moving forward.

"We were very deliberate about the reps that he was going to get, and how he was going to be used," Fleury said. "He didn't play in the preseason. It was the very first NFL game, huge stage. We wanted to be cautious in terms of his workload. He earned more reps moving forward, and we'll continue to bring him along and develop him the right way.”

Fleury explained that the limited use of Price had nothing to do with "anything physical." Said Fleury, "It’s just being a rookie.”

With Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III gone in free agency and Zach Charbonnet out for at least the first four games as he continues to recover from an ACL tear suffered in the divisional-round win over the 49ers, Price is the top tailback.

With his 24 reps in the season opener, Price had 10 carries for 52 yards and two catches for six yards. The next opportunity comes in Arizona on Sunday, against the 1-0 Cardinals.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Josh Allen, Bills running over Lions, up 27-10 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bills quarterback has thrown three touchdowns and run for another.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills have christened their new stadium with champagne and caviar on the field.

Josh Allen threw three touchdowns in the first half and ran for another, and the Bills are in the locker room at halftime with a 27-10 lead.

Almost everything went right for the Bills in the first half other than Tyler Bass missing an extra point, punting on their fourth possession and injuries to wide receivers DJ Moore and Keon Coleman. Moore is in the X-ray room being examined for a shoulder injury and a stinger, and Coleman returned after getting his right ankle taped on the sideline.

The Bills have outgained the Lions 299 to 155, scoring touchdowns on their first four possessions on drives of 85, 79, 57 and 68 yards.

Allen is 12-of-19 for 164 yards with three touchdowns on throws of 43 yards to Josh Palmer, 1 yard to Dawson Knox and 16 yards to Dalton Kincaid, The quarterback also has four carries for 40 yards and a touchdown.

James Cook already has 100 yards, rushing for 101 on 11 carries. Kincaid has five catches for 65 yards.

Jared Goff kept his streak of consecutive games with a touchdown alive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to running back Jahmyr Gibbs. It was the 25th game in a row Goff has thrown a TD pass. But it came with the Lions down 21-0.

Goff is 11-of-16 for 128 yards and a touchdown. He's been sacked three times, including twice by Greg Rousseau, who is off to a great start this season. Gibbs has rushed for 47 yards on eight carries and has caught four passes for 40 yards.

item.title: Korn Ferry tries to keep key document in Brian Flores case under seal
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Brian Flores litigation has uncovered a potentially significant document through a subpoena issued to the Korn Ferry search firm.
item.content:encoded:
The Brian Flores litigation has uncovered a potentially significant document through a subpoena issued to the Korn Ferry search firm. And Korn Ferry is trying to keep the document out of public view.

The document has been designated as confidential under a general protective order that allows the parties to claim that certain materials should not be disclosed. Flores's lawyers have challenged the effort to keep it secret.

Via Daniel Kaplan, Korn Ferry filed paperwork on Thursday in support of the effort to keep the document under seal. Korn Ferry argues, among other things, that “whether the limited information from Exhibit A that Korn Ferry requests remain sealed is purportedly `discriminatory’ or `retaliatory,’ such that it supports and is relevant to Plaintiff’s claims in the Supplemental Complaint, has no bearing on whether Korn Ferry is legally entitled to have Exhibit A remain under seal.”

This statement suggests, as Kaplan notes, that Flores's lawyers have argued that the document helps prove that he was the victim of discrimination and/or retaliation.

The document in question, which one source called "insane," was generated by Korn Ferry in connection with a coaching search conducted by the Raiders. The precise Raiders coaching search isn’t specified; the Raiders have hired new coaches in 2026, 2025, 2024, 2022, and 2018.

If the document shows potential retaliation, it means that it came from a coaching search after the filing of Flores's lawsuit, on February 1, 2022. Because the Raiders hired Josh McDaniels on January 31, 2022, it would limit the potential application of the document to the search that resulted in the hiring of Antonio Pierce in 2024, Pete Carroll in 2025, or Klint Kubiak in 2026.

Two of those searches happened after Tom Brady — who played for the Patriots when Flores served on the coaching staff there — became a minority owner of the team.

Regardless of whether the document comes to light in the short term, it'll definitely be disclosed and discussed if/when the case goes to trial. If the document is truly bad for the NFL and the various teams that have been sued, it could result in the case being settled before the document ever comes to light.

item.content:encoded:
The Bills are having a grand ol' time in their new stadium.

Buffalo has scored three touchdowns on three possessions in the new Highmark Stadium, taking a 21-0 lead over the Lions.

The Bills have outgained the Lions 209 to 10, with three possessions to two.

Josh Allen threw his second touchdown, finding Dawson Knox for a 1-yard score. The quarterback had his choice whether to run it in or throw it to Knox. He took care of his tight end.

Allen scored on a 1-yard run on the Bills' first possession and threw a 43-yard touchdown pass to Josh Palmer on the second.

As if things weren't bad enough for the Lions, defensive back Avonte Maddox was carted off the field in the second quarter. The team lists him as questionable to return with a foot injury.

item.title: Rams officially place Myles Garrett on injured reserve
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Rams have made one of their expected roster moves official on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams have made one of their expected roster moves official on Thursday.

Myles Garrett has been placed on injured reserve, Los Angeles announced.

It was reported on Sunday that Garrett would have knee surgery and be placed on IR after an ineffective performance to start the season in the loss to the 49ers.

Head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that the team had believed that Garrett's knee injury was something he could work through.

Now, Garrett is officially out for at least the next four weeks.

The Rams did not announce a corresponding move, leaving a roster spot open.

The Rams will host the Giants on Monday night.

item.title: Hall of Fame announces its new group of voters
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The recent overhaul of the Hall of Fame selection process includes a dramatic reduction in the number of voters, from 50 down to 28.
item.content:encoded:
The recent overhaul of the Hall of Fame selection process includes a dramatic reduction in the number of voters, from 50 down to 28.

On Thursday, the Hall of Fame announced the new group of voters.

They are: Hall of Famer Jared Allen, Howard Balzer of USA Today, Jarrett Bell of USA Today, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press, Vic Carucci of WGRZ-TV, Mike Chappell of CBS4/Fox59, Pete Dougherty of the Green Bay Press-Gazette, Jeff Duncan of the New Orleans Times-Picayune, Hall of Famer Dan Fouts, Scott Garceau of WMAR-TV, Bob Glauber, Vahe Gregorian of the Kansas City Star, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic, Lindsay Jones of The Ringer, Ira Kaufman of JoeBucsFan.com, Ross Ketover of NFL Films, Sam Kouvaris, Jeff Legwold of ESPN, Rob Maadi of the Associated Press, Gary Myers, Sal Paolantonio of ESPN, Dan Pompei of The Athletic, Mike Sando of The Athletic, Hall of Famer Will Shields, Jim Trotter, Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News, Eric Williams of Fox Sports, and Charean Williams of PFT.

There's no apparent rhyme or reason regarding the decisions made to keep and to cut loose members from the former panel of 50. If anything, fewer voters can create more problems because it takes a smaller group to screw things up.

But it wouldn't be the first time that the nameless, faceless folks who control the Hall of Fame screwed something up. It would simply be the latest.

item.title: Sean McVay "hopeful" Aaron Donald will play this week
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Giants expect Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald to play on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants expect Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald to play on Monday night. Rams coach Sean McVay is "hopeful."

McVay said before practice that Donald would fully participate on Thursday, and indeed, Donald is not on the team's injury report. (Donald's roster exemption was lifted Friday.)

Donald did not travel to Australia with the team, staying at home to continue working his way back from a two-year absence from football. He participated in individual drills for the first time on Aug. 30 and joined team drills on Sept. 6.

McVay said the Rams are not looking for specific benchmarks to determine whether Donald plays for the first time since 2023.

"It's more along the line of how does he feel?" McVay said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN.

Donald is "obviously champing at the bit" to play, but the Rams' travel schedule to Australia has prevented limited practice opportunities for Donald.

"But what we are hopeful is, is that we'll have some good work today and tomorrow and then hopefully he's feeling good enough and if he says he's ready to go, then we'll be excited to see him," McVay said.

Rams defensive end Myles Garrett is "feeling good" after knee surgery on Monday, but the reigning Defensive Player of the Year has no timeline for his return. Garrett was on crutches on Wednesday and walking without them Thursday.

Because Garrett is on injured reserve, he will miss at least the next four games.

"We're not going to rush him back," McVay said. "We want to make sure that he's feeling good, he's able to get out on the practice field, do all the things that are necessary for him to perform at a level that he's been accustomed to."
